rules.statement: RETIRED from automated enforcement (#853). Its GlobGate mechanism (patterns vs. this rule's own scope.applies_to) was structurally disjoint: the paths this rule's scope could ever hand to the engine could never overlap with the paths named in its own forbidden-patterns list, so the rule could never fire regardless of file content -- confirmed empirically, not merely suspected. The real, load-bearing lane-boundary control CORE actually runs is autonomy.proposals.safe_auto_approval_envelope below, which governs a narrower and more precise claim: not 'agents cannot write outside a lane' in the abstract, but exactly which atomic actions and which repository-relative paths a proposal may target for AUTONOMOUS (non-human) approval. This rule no longer dispatches to a mapping. Historical marker only -- see rationale.
rules.rationale: Found during #842 Unit E (G2 fixture-coverage program), filed as #853: GlobGateEngine.verify()'s generic pattern-matcher does read `patterns` and does flag a match as a violation -- this was not a missing-dispatch defect like #852's rules. The defect was that the rule's own `scope.applies_to` (src/will/agents/**/*.py) and its `patterns` list (src/body/cli/logic/**, src/features/introspection/**, src/features/self_healing/**) are two disjoint directory trees: no file the audit engine would ever hand to verify() under this rule's scope could ever match a pattern in the forbidden list, and no file matching a pattern in the list falls within this rule's own scope, so the rule always reported clean regardless of actual agent write behavior. The mapping's own comment described `patterns` as the *allowed* lanes ('Only allow agents to modify non-core directories autonomously'), while the engine's semantics treat anything in `patterns` as *forbidden* -- a second, independent contradiction on top of the disjoint-scope defect. Retired rather than repaired: 'agents must not write outside their lane' in the abstract has no single mechanically decidable definition (which lane, whose lane, checked how), whereas the concrete, governor-decided claim this system actually needs enforced -- the safe-auto-approval action-and-path envelope -- is precise, real, and now genuinely running. Retired rather than deleted so the prior declaration stays traceable. Its mapping entry is removed.

rules.statement: A proposal MUST NOT transition to status='approved' under approval_authority='risk_classification.safe_auto_approval' unless every one of its actions references an action_id in the independently governed safe_auto_approval_envelope (.intent/enforcement/config/action_risk.yaml), targets a repository-relative Python file under src/ or tests/ (direct or nested children, no absolute path, no traversal segment), and the set of those target paths exactly matches the proposal's declared ProposalScope.files. No ProposalAction naming flow_id satisfies this rule -- no flow is authorized for safe auto-approval, including test-generation flows. This rule does not constrain approval_authority='principal.governor': a human governor's approval may cross this envelope; the envelope binds only the autonomous approval path.
rules.rationale: #853: impact_level: safe classification in action_risk.yaml is a RISK tier, not an AUTHORIZATION grant -- several impact_level: safe actions (build.test_for_symbol, check.imports, admin.meta, claim.proposal, ...) were never meant to auto-execute without a human step, yet nothing previously stopped ProposalStateManager.approve() from accepting approval_authority='risk_classification.safe_auto_approval' for any proposal regardless of which actions or paths it actually named -- the only prior checks were the approval_authority closed-vocabulary check and the ADR-109 assisted-lane validation gate, neither of which examined the proposal's actions or scope at all. A proposal's self-declared ProposalScope was similarly never independently verified against what its actions actually targeted. This rule closes that gap with a real, governor-decided envelope: exactly five atomic actions (fix.imports, fix.ids, fix.logging, fix.headers, fix.format), Python files under src/ or tests/ only, no flows. Enforcement is deterministic and runs on every safe-auto-approval attempt via ProposalStateManager.approve() -- see will.autonomy.safe_auto_approval_envelope.validate_envelope. A denial leaves the proposal in DRAFT for principal.governor review; it is never silently rejected, deleted, or rolled back.

rules.statement: All non-trivial autonomous decisions MUST produce an inspectable trace in the Decision Log.
The RemediationMap MUST NOT dispatch any entry whose confidence value is below 0.80. Entries below this threshold MUST NOT produce Proposals regardless of their status field.

The ConservationGate MUST reject any LLM-produced code whose logical token preservation ratio falls below 0.50 of the original, unless the invoking Proposal explicitly declares deletions_authorized=True.
The PlannerAgent MUST explicitly reference its governing quality assurance policy.

scope.notes: Scoped to PlannerAgent only -- the sole autonomous component responsible for policy-aligned planning decisions.
